admission.justification: A future performance cut must not silently omit file entries from marks classification or read every file eagerly before a view requests its marks.

alternatives.option: Keep the complete per-file entry classification and read/share it when an admitted view drawing that file marks opens.
alternatives.reason: Appendix151 explicitly chooses the per-file population and on-demand boundary. useMarkClassification honors active/listed/supplied state and the scope shares a changed path pending/ready answer; the native per-file projection returns both side entry populations.

alternatives.option: Cap or trim the per-file entry population, or eagerly classify unrelated files solely to avoid this admitted on-demand response.
alternatives.reason: Trimming hides potentially deciding entries; eager unrelated reads abandon the chosen file/view acquisition boundary rather than improving its implementation.
alternatives.reconsider_when: An approved requirement specifies a truthful paged/alternative complete entry contract and how marks remain complete without speculative reads.

consequences: A future performance cut must not silently omit file entries from marks classification or read every file eagerly before a view requests its marks.
No obligation to read marks for unchanged or unlisted paths, no unconditional single network request across failures/scopes, and no bound on every response size or a semantic grade.
context: Approved MIK-R57@v2 appendix83/151 and rule6 require this by-design choice to be recorded, not deferred as a gap. Source obligation: MIK-R57@v2 by-design classification-scope. This is the requirement-prescribed boundary, not a claim that an undocumented alternative was seriously weighed.
decider: Approved MIK-R57@v2 under D18/D47/D48; Curator records the specified boundary under constrains_future_work.
